subject: Renewal conversation: Orchid.ai — surge capacity, term options & save path
messages:
From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@orchid.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Chen <leah.chen@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick sync on renewal — unexpected token surge and capacity question

Hi Maya,

Hope you’re doing well — we’ve been seeing a 3x token surge across our recommendation pipeline the last six weeks (attached sample), and our finance team flagged that our current committed tier will be exhausted well before the anniversary. Before we start a formal RFP, wanted to understand options on your side for:

- Short-term top-up capacity for the next 60 days
- Mid-contract term addendum for an accelerated usage tier (we’d prefer to avoid a full reprocurement)
- Any bakeoff assistance if we need to validate other vendors (time is tight).

Can we schedule a 30-min call this week? Leah and our procurement lead are on copy.

Thanks,
Sam
Samuel Park
Head of ML Platform, Orchid.ai

Attachments: orchid_usage_oct2026.csv (CSV sample, 120KB)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@orchid.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync on renewal — unexpected token surge and capacity question

Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and for the data. I’m sorry you’re hitting this ramp unexpectedly. Short answer: we have a couple of paths that don’t require a reprocurement:

1) Short-term burst pool: a metered top-up for 30–90 days to cover immediate runway while we size uplift.
2) Mid-term amendment: add a tier with a 30–60% unit discount for committed additional capacity (6–12 month addendum).
3) Bakeoff support: we’ll share an operational checklist and can run a controlled side-by-side on our infra with fixed workloads — our engineering team will help execute.

I copied Lauren (sales lead) and Priyom (solutions) so we can align on pricing and the ops plan. Are you free Friday 11/7 at 11am PT? I can get a short SLA amendment draft and a usage readout pre-call.

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Account Exec — Strategic West, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.com

Attachments: (will send SLA draft & pricing workbook before the call)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@orchid.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync on renewal — unexpected token surge and capacity question

Hi Sam — looping in Rishi (renewals lead) to clear any internal escalation.

We ran a quick cost model and attached a starter pricing workbook with two options: 1) 90-day burst credit (cust pays metered overage, no contract change), and 2) Commitment addendum: +50% committed capacity at a blended discounted rate with a 9-month term.

We’ll be explicit about performance parity guarantees and operational playbooks if you opt for the addendum (cold-start limits, caching expectations, KV sizing).

If you can confirm Friday 11/7 11am PT, we’ll send a proposed amendment PDF and a concise runbook for the bakeoff.

Best,
Lauren
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_workbook_orchid.xlsx

From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@orchid.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Chen <leah.chen@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync on renewal — unexpected token surge and capacity question

Thanks — 11am PT on 11/7 works. Quick follow-ups before we talk:

- Can you share the SLA amendment draft so our security/compliance folks can eyeball it ahead of time?
- The procurement lead wants to know if a mid-term addendum would lock us into a minimum commit that prevents us from trying a small PoC with a competitor. We need clear escape/fallback language.

Leah — joining the call; procurement will jump in during the pricing portion.

Sam

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@orchid.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: bakeoff plan and SLA draft attached

Hi all — following our call on 11/7, attaching the SLA amendment v1 and a short bakeoff runbook. Key notes:

- SLA amendment v1 includes a 99.5% p99 target and a scoped maintenance window allowance for burst scaling.
- Addendum term example: 9 months additional commit with a 50% step-up; cancellation allowed with 60-day notice and prorated refund on unused commit if migration occurs to an alternate provider after a minimum 90-day notice period.
- Bakeoff plan: 72-hour controlled run with our side-by-side harness. Redwood will run the reference workload, Orchid provides sanitized dataset and validation prompts.

Sam — please pass this to your security and procurement. We also included a pricing sheet option (conservative vs aggressive uplift).

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_amendment_v1.pdf; pricing_workbook_orchid.xlsx

From: Leah Chen <leah.chen@orchid.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Park <samuel.park@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: Orchid.ai — surge capacity, term options & save path

Hi team — procurement reviewed the amendment and had two asks: 1) tighten the migration refund clause so Orchid gets a prorated credit for unused commit if we legitimately move within the first 120 days (they want faster credits), and 2) explicit cross-vendor bakeoff neutrality language (no exclusivity). If we can get those two edits, procurement is open to the 9-month addendum.

Also, security flagged a small logging retention query — can Redwood confirm exportable audit logs for the addendum period? If yes, we’re inclined to sign quickly.

Sam/Leah
